- Work directly with customers and turn recurring pain into product improvements.

- Technical credibility to engage deeply in architecture and incidents without owning daily implementation.

- A record of hiring, coaching, developing, and retaining engineers, including senior ICs.

- Strong execution judgment across ambiguity, parallel workstreams, risk, and long-term system health.

- A customer mindset, strong Product partnership, clear communication, and distributed-team leadership.

- Influence the product, roadmap, operating model, and customer outcomes.

title: Director of Power Business Real Estate
description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Director, Power Business Real Estate to join our team. 

Position Description

The Director, Power Business Real Estate owns all site control activities for Oklo's Aurora powerhouse development pipeline. Site control is the first gate in the development lifecycle and a prerequisite for every downstream discipline. Over time, you will lead a team of Senior Land Managers and Analysts responsible for identifying, evaluating, and securing sites across multiple geographies. You report to the VP of Origination and coordinate closely with the VP of Development, Director of Project Development, and Oklo's Environmental & Permitting team on site feasibility and regulatory compatibility.

Specific responsibilities may include:

• Lead all site identification, screening, and acquisition efforts across Oklo's development pipeline

• Negotiate and execute land option agreements, purchase and sale agreements, easements, rights-of-way, access agreements, and Joint Venture agreements

• Manage title review, survey coordination, and curative title work across active sites

• Build and maintain a pipeline of prospective sites meeting Oklo's siting criteria (proximity to load, available land area, soil conditions, water access, community context)

• Coordinate with Development Engineering on site feasibility and with Oklo's Environmental & Permitting team on zoning and land use risk

• Manage landowner and broker relationships across multiple states

• Over time, build and lead a team of land and real estate professionals

• Identify and secure sites suitable for Isotope production facilities, evaluating proximity to Aurora powerhouse sites, workforce access, water and waste infrastructure, and compatibility with NRC facility licensing requirements

• Lead land and real estate activities for Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses (NLICs), including multi-parcel assemblage, shared infrastructure easement structuring, and coordination with local governments on zoning for mixed nuclear-use facilities

Minimum Qualifications:

• 10+ years in energy project land acquisition, real estate, or land management

• Demonstrated experience executing site control across a portfolio of complex energy or infrastructure projects

• Strong negotiation skills with experience across agricultural, industrial, and government-owned land

• Familiarity with GIS tools for site screening and parcel analysis

• Experience working in multi-state environments with varying regulatory and title requirements

Competencies

We are looking for a Director of Power Business Real Estate that is:

• Passionate about clean energy 

• Passionate about making advanced fission a reality

• Willing and able to learn quickly

• Eager to work on a dynamic team, receive constructive feedback, and grow with us

title: Senior Regulatory Analyst and Writer
description:
Location: Remote, United States. Core availability 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern, Monday through Friday.
Type: Full time, salaried.
Eligibility: U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident.
The role
This is the analytical center of the contract and the face of it to the client. When a comment period closes on a proposed Packers and Stockyards Act rule, you are the person who reads what the public sent in, works out what actually matters in it, and turns thousands of pages into something the agency's policy staff can use to write a final rule.
Between rulemakings you run the contract: the deliverable tracking, the monthly reporting, the weekly client meetings, and the readiness work that makes the next sprint survivable. You will also direct the analyst bench during comment closes, setting the coding scheme and reviewing what comes back.
The turnaround is fifteen calendar days from the close of the comment period for both the substantive analysis and the key issues matrix, and the client has signaled they may want it faster. This job suits someone who does careful work quickly and does not need to be managed through a deadline.
Analysis and writing

• Analyze public comments submitted on proposed rules, identifying themes, high-risk issues, quantitative metrics such as comment counts by topic, recommendations from the public, and the line between substantive and non-substantive submissions.

• Distinguish organized form-letter campaigns from unique substantive comments and account for both in the analysis.

• Identify every issue raised through public comment and build the key issues matrix, with comments sorted and categorized by issue for policy discussion and for drafting written responses in the final rule.

• Engage in DFT/DFM reviews with electrical engineering and product firmware teams.

• BS or MS in CS/CE/EE or equivalent industry experience

• Strong C coding ability for embedded systems

• Experience integrating microcontrollers with analog and digital sensors

• Experience developing firmware in bare-metal, RTOS environments, and embedded Linux

• Solid understanding and application of coding best practices, board bring up and debugging

• Some familiarity with common bus protocols such as USB, SPI, I2C, CAN, RS232, RS485, Ethernet, etc.

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance 

•

title: Principal Scientist / Associate Director, Soft Materials Experimentation
description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila is hiring a Scientific Leader to build and run our experimental soft materials team, covering formulations, polymers, colloids, gels, emulsions, inks, adhesives, and coatings. You will take on a group of four scientists and grow it as the portfolio expands across formulation, rheological and scattering characterization, and polymer processing. The team turns soft-matter problems into closed-loop autonomous workflows: defining what gets measured, how it gets measured at throughput, and how the resulting data supports active learning and inverse design. The work asks you to stay close to the bench while mentoring a growing team and setting its direction over a multi-year growth horizon.

What You'll Be Building

• Lead and grow a group of scientists spanning formulation, polymer processing, and physical characterization; set scientific direction, develop the team, and hire against an expanding portfolio

• Own the experimental strategy for soft materials - the measurement stack, the campaign designs, and the scientific validity of what the group publishes internally and to partners

• Hold your team's delivery on partner-funded programs alongside the technical program managers who own the programs themselves, setting the standard on timelines, throughput, and data quality

As a Vehicle Integration Lead at Wayve, you’ll provide technical leadership for the electrical architecture, integration, validation and delivery of our autonomous driving systems across vehicle platforms.

This role sits at the intersection of electrical and mechanical engineering, vehicle systems, autonomous driving hardware, software and integration. You’ll lead the integration of compute, sensing, power, communications and supporting hardware into development and production-intent vehicles, ensuring systems perform reliably and safely in real-world environments.

You’ll work closely with Systems Engineering, Embedded Software, Autonomy, Safety, Vehicle Operations, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, OEM partners and external suppliers. You’ll also partner directly with OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers, contract manufacturers, upfitters and integration partners to resolve technical challenges and move programs toward production readiness.
